title: One Garment, One Ticket: Marlowe & Finch Alterations Ticket Rule
content:
**Clause.** A customer of Marlowe & Finch Alterations may hold any number of alteration tickets; there is no maximum number of tickets per customer. Each ticket covers one garment, so a suit jacket and its trousers are two tickets. Prices, turnaround, deposits, fittings, remakes and complimentary work are decided per ticket.

## The clause point by point

| Question the rule answers | Answer |
|---|---|
| How many tickets may one customer have open or on record? | Any number; no limit applies. |
| How many garments does one ticket cover? | One. |
| Is a two-piece suit one ticket or two? | Two: one for the jacket, one for the trousers. |
| At what level are prices, turnaround, deposits, fittings, remakes and complimentary work decided? | Ticket by ticket. |

## Hypothetical illustration

A customer leaves a suit jacket, its matching trousers and a dress at the same Marlowe & Finch Alterations shop on one visit. Three tickets are opened. Each ticket has its own price, its own promised date, its own deposit treatment, its own included fittings, its own remake allowance and its own complimentary-work decision.
